source_review.notes: Checked every structured reference live. Four Kimball Group SCD sources, three current Microsoft Fabric dimension/load sources, and current PostgreSQL range/constraint documentation each returned HTTP 200. Claims about Types 1, 2, 4–7, surrogate stability, inferred members, effective intervals and database nonoverlap mechanisms are scoped to those sources.

evidence: Reviewed durable-key version sets V_b, surrogate map k(v), attribute map A(v), half-open valid intervals I(v), optional system intervals J(v), containment, overlap and fact-resolution relation rho(b,t).
Checked quantifiers for nonempty/nonoverlapping versions, at-most-one uniqueness, exactly-one coverage and current-version mapping c(b).
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates identity, valid time, system time, uniqueness and coverage rather than treating them as one property.

evidence: Executed scd-as-of-resolution with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced 2 versions, 1 current version, 0 overlaps and surrogate resolution [101,102,102].
Independently checked February 15 in [Jan 1,Mar 1), and March 1/April 1 in [Mar 1,infinity).
Recomputed historical totals North=40 and West=60+20=80, current West=40+60+20=120, with equal grand totals.
Confirmed ISO YYYY-MM-DD lexical ordering is valid within the fixture's fixed normalized date representation.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The executable fixture uses exact dates and integers only; it does not model timezones, sub-day precision or database transactions.

evidence: Re-derived half-open containment s<=t<e and overlap iff max starts is less than min ends.
Verified adjacent [a,b) and [b,c) intervals are disjoint while b resolves to the second interval.
Re-derived uniqueness by contradiction: two simultaneous resolutions imply a nonempty interval intersection.
Checked that uniqueness yields at most one match and requires a separate coverage premise for exactly one.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Infinity/sentinel handling is abstracted in the equations and concretized consistently in the fixture.

evidence: Reviewed empty, adjacent, gapped, overlapping, inverted and open intervals plus facts before first start, at boundaries and after closure.
Reviewed no-op changes, normalized-value changes, reversions, same-effective-time conflicts, unstable hashes and source-sequence duplicates.
Reviewed inferred/unknown/not-applicable/error members, late details, late business changes, corrections, deletes, inactivity, erasure, merges, splits and source-key reuse.
Reviewed Types 0–7, volatile profile cardinality, partial Type 6 updates and unsafe Type 7 durable-key fanout.
Reviewed valid versus system time, atomic expire/insert, concurrent retries, aggregate refresh and irrecoverable Type 1 history.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Each edge case has a named business decision, rejection/quarantine path, or validation/reconciliation requirement.

evidence: Traced identity, interval, current, resolution, stability, attribute-policy, perspective, audit, atomicity and reconciliation invariants through the sixteen-step mechanism.
Checked all ten examples for durable/surrogate identity, effective-time selection and explicit current/historical behavior.
Confirmed every eligible fact path demands exactly one member and every dual-perspective path preserves population before comparing grand totals.
invariant_checking.notes: The module consistently distinguishes business requirements from SCD numeric labels and database implementation.

evidence: Verified that assuming two resolved versions at t directly makes t an element of their intersection, contradicting pairwise nonoverlap.
Verified boundary membership for [a,b) and [b,c) without requiring a precision-dependent predecessor instant.
Confirmed the proof explicitly does not infer existence/coverage from uniqueness.
proof_review.notes: The proof establishes only unique as-of resolution under same durable key, normalized time and nonoverlap premises.

evidence: The uniqueness argument is explicitly labeled 'Proof sketch — disjoint half-open intervals guarantee unique as-of resolution.'
Other mathematical expressions are definitions/invariants and do not claim external formal verification.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Scope and the separate coverage limitation are adjacent to the labeled sketch.

evidence: The executable example is labeled as an ISO-date exact-integer demonstration, not database concurrency or production evidence.
Worked scenarios are synthetic and operational recommendations request measurement rather than reporting invented prevalence or performance.
Platform documentation is cited for capabilities without claiming those capabilities are universally enforced.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production accuracy, latency, scale, legal compliance or optimizer result is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed attribute-level SCD selection, Types 0–7, durable versus surrogate identity, valid versus system time, as-was versus as-is reporting, inferred members, corrections and entity relationship changes. Type 2 is correctly distinguished from bitemporal/event history.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed row fields, canonical change detection, half-open intervals, nonoverlap/current constraints, fact resolution, idempotency, atomic publication, late interval surgery, aggregate refresh, monitoring and migration. The workflow yields actionable DDL/data tests, load behavior and consumer contracts.

pedagogical_review.notes: The chapter develops SCDs from business questions through interval algebra and operational handling. The executable boundary fixture contrasts historical/current rollups; ten examples cover common errors; five exercises progress from attribute classification to late changes, hybrid designs and an information-limited migration with complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only. No external academic, Kimball Group, Microsoft, PostgreSQL, data-warehouse practitioner, legal, privacy, accounting or production review is claimed. The pure-Python fixture does not validate database temporal constraints, transactional isolation, concurrent surrogate allocation, timezone conversion, high-volume history, semantic-tool relationships or organization-specific retention policy.
